plan: [Second-price sealed-bid: you pay the second-highest bid. With affiliated signals there is a winner's-curse risk, but the Vickrey format largely protects truthful bidders because payment depends on others' bids, not your own. No history to learn from in this single round, so avoid unnecessary shading that loses profitable wins. Bid my private value to win whenever the market price is below my value and avoid leaving expected surplus on the table.]

[I treat this as a second-price (Vickrey) auction: bidding your true private value maximizes expected surplus in the standard case and avoids over- or underbidding when signals are symmetric. With one round and no learning, shading is unlikely to help because others’ bids only inform about the common component I can't observe. My private value is $17, so I bid that (in $0.1 increments) to capture any positive surplus if I win while avoiding systematic loss.]

[This is a sealed-bid second-price auction. In the private-value case bidding your value is dominant; with the common-value component there is affiliation, but I have no past rounds to learn from and values redraw each round. To avoid the winner's curse and maximize long-run profit, I will bid my true private value ($9). This prevents overpaying while capturing positive surplus when I win.]
